questions.question: A process has 8 unknown variables and 5 independent equations. The degrees of freedom of the system are:
questions.explanation: Degrees of freedom = number of unknowns − number of independent equations = 8 − 5 = 3, so the problem is under-specified and three more specifications are needed.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.topic: Material Balance without Reaction, Recycle, Bypass and Purge
questions.subtopic: Process calculations: balances, recycle, bypass, purge
questions.question: A system is correctly specified (exactly solvable) when the degrees of freedom are:
options: Equal to the number of streams
questions.explanation: Zero degrees of freedom means as many independent equations as unknowns; positive means under-specified and negative means over-specified.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: A tie component in material balance calculations is a component that:
options: Passes from one stream to another unchanged, without reacting or accumulating
questions.explanation: Tie components such as nitrogen in combustion air or ash in coal link streams, which simplifies the balance.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The main purpose of a purge stream in a reactor system with recycle is to:
options: Remove inert or by-product build-up in the recycle loop
questions.explanation: Without a purge, inerts that enter with the feed would accumulate in the loop and stop the process.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: A stream that skips one or more process units and rejoins downstream is called:
questions.explanation: Bypass stream sends part of the feed around a unit to control composition or temperature; recycle returns product to an earlier unit.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: For a steady-state process with chemical reaction, the general material balance on a component is:
questions.explanation: At steady state accumulation is zero; for a reactive component, generation and consumption by reaction must be included.

questions.question: In a process with fresh feed 100 mol/h of A, single-pass conversion 25 per cent to B and complete separation with recycle of all unreacted A, the flow of A entering the reactor is:
questions.explanation: Overall conversion is 100 per cent, so 100 mol/h of B is formed. If 25 per cent of the reactor feed reacts, reactor feed = 100/0.25 = 400 mol/h, and the recycle is 300 mol/h.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: If 100 kg of 20 per cent NaCl solution is mixed with 300 kg of 40 per cent NaCl solution, the mass percent of NaCl in the mixture is:
questions.explanation: Salt = 20 + 120 = 140 kg in 400 kg of solution, i.e., 35 per cent.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: An evaporator receives 1000 kg/h of a solution containing 10 per cent solids and produces a thick liquor with 40 per cent solids. The water evaporated is:
questions.explanation: Solids = 100 kg/h. Product = 100/0.40 = 250 kg/h, so water removed = 1000 − 250 = 750 kg/h.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: A feed of 200 kg/h splits so that 25 per cent bypasses a reactor. The flow to the reactor is:
questions.explanation: Bypass = 0.25 × 200 = 50 kg/h, leaving 150 kg/h to the reactor.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: A solution contains 30 per cent NaOH by mass in water (NaOH = 40, H2O = 18). The mole percent of NaOH is about:
questions.explanation: On a 100 g basis: NaOH = 30/40 = 0.75 mol; water = 70/18 = 3.89 mol; total 4.64 mol; mole fraction = 0.75/4.64 = 16.2 per cent.
